Method of Attack: Encrypts data using AES encryption and demands ransom in bitcoins
Encrypts files on local drives and unmapped network shares
Deletes Shadow Volume Copies using vssadmin.exe to prevent file recovery
Changes filenames of encrypted files to a unique format
Installs via malicious Word document attachments with macros in phishing emails
Macros download and execute Locky ransomware executable from remote server
Creates ransom notes and changes desktop wallpaper with ransom instructions
Stores unique victim ID, RSA public key, and ransom note text in Windows registry
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with malicious Word document attachments containing macros
Execution of downloaded ransomware executable from macro
Network shares (including unmapped shares) accessible to victim machine
Indicators of Compromise: Emails with subject similar to 'ATTN: Invoice J-98223146'
Encrypted files renamed to format '[unique_id][identifier].locky', e.g. 'F67091F1D24A922B1A7FC27E19A9D9BC.locky'
Ransom notes named '_Locky_recover_instructions.txt' in affected folders
Tor site URL: 6dtxgqam4crv6rr6.onion for decrypter page
Executable stored in %Temp% folder with random name and executed
Impacted Systems: Windows systems with local drives and network shares
Systems with accessible unmapped network shares
Discoverer: Not explicitly stated in the source content
